title: Plant Billing Basis for the Crop Input Purchasing Accounts: Invoice, Due Date and Price on the Day
content:
An invoice on a Crop Input Purchasing Account is raised when product physically leaves the plant, on the delivery ticket, and never when an order is merely written.

## 1. Dating the invoice

1.1 The invoice date is the day of that delivery, and the due date is the invoice date plus the account's terms in calendar days, a payment landing on the due date itself still being on time.

1.2 Where the terms day falls on a day the office is shut the due date moves to the next day the office is open.

1.3 Where the terms carry past the end of a month onto a day that month does not have, the due date falls on the last day of that month.

## 2. Pricing

2.1 Product is priced at the list price in force on the day of delivery.

2.2 The words that stood here — *"except where the line draws against a prepay booking, which prices at the booked price however the list has moved"* — are **no longer in force** on the Crop Input Purchasing Accounts, having been superseded by the current basis on which a prepay booking prices what is drawn against it.

## 3. Cash programmes

3.1 Cash programmes are paid for as the product leaves and carry no terms at all, so an invoice on a cash programme is raised and settled the same day.

## 4. Charges billed with the product

4.1 A delivery under the programme's minimum order carries the delivery minimum charge, and splitting one order across two fields or two delivery days carries the split load charge, both of which are billed on the same invoice as the product rather than separately. The minimum order, the under-minimum charge and the split load charge are each the figure the member's programme carries in the delivery tariff.

4.2 The extended amount of a line is the quantity multiplied by the unit price, rounded to two decimal places.

## 5. Prescription products

5.1 Prescription products are not released at all on programmes that require a current soil test until one is on file. This is tested before the product is released, on the cooperative's own record of the request the member lodged — the kind of request it is, the stage it stands at and its own reference number — read together with the programme the account is held under.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

A delivery is made on the 4th day of a month on a programme carrying terms of 30 calendar days. The due date falls on the 4th day of the following month, and a payment landing on that day is on time; a payment landing the day after is not.

A delivery is made on the 31st day of a month on the same terms, and the month the due date would fall in has only 30 days: the due date falls on the last day of that month.

superseded_clauses: except where the line draws against a prepay booking, which prices at the booked price however the list has moved
